run.agent: a fresh Claude Haiku subagent with no other context
run.rule: read only the guide, open no other file, run no command, answer from the page alone
run.questions: WR11_QUESTIONS in wr11.ts, asked word for word

answers.stair: Draw the stair as a room with use `stair` on every floor it joins, in the same place, with an opening or door from the hall or landing on each floor. Put `through first` on the room line to write it once and stand it on every floor from its own up to `first`. The flight itself (treads, width, walking line) is optional and goes in the plan file's `stairs` list, not in rooms text. The guide's example uses floors `ground` (level 0) and `first` (level 1).
answers.office: Give it the use `office`, and keep the person's own word in the name, for example `room office "My office" office 3.0 x 3.0 ...`. The guide reads `office` as the use, and the room's name keeps the person's word.
answers.toilet: Give it the use `toilet`, and keep the person's word in the name, for example `room loo "Loo" toilet 1.5 x 1.8 ...`. The guide lists `loo` as a word also read as `toilet`, and the name keeps the person's own word.
answers.inside-outside: A room's size is inside by default: to the inside faces of its walls, east-west by north-south. To write a size measured to the outside faces, put `outside` after the size on the room line, for example `room living "Living room" living 4.0 x 5.0 outside at 0,0`. Grid then measures it to the outside faces; `sizes outside` on its own line makes outside the default for every room after it.
answers.dividing-line: No, the dividing line has no thickness. Write `open` at the end of the room line to divide it from the room it is placed against, for example `room kitchen "Kitchen" kitchen 3.0 x 4.5 east of living open`. For any other pair, write `wall between <room> and <room> virtual`. Grid draws it dashed as a virtual wall, with thickness 0 in the plan file.
answers.l-shaped: It is one room, written with `polygon` and the corners of its inside faces in order round it, in metres. For example: `room living "Living room" living polygon 0,0 6,0 6,3 3,3 3,5 0,5`. Do not split it into two rooms to draw the L.
